title: UPL Eg II eggplant: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: UPL Eg II eggplant: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: UPL Eg II eggplant is an eggplant variety. 79 to 86 days to harvest, 15.5 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: UPL Eg II is a registered eggplant variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1980. UPLB bred it. It takes 79 to 86 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 15.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 79 to 86 days from transplanting to the first harvest.
**Yield:** 15.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about UPL Eg II eggplant
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

UPL Eg II eggplant takes 79 to 86 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is about the average of the 9 eggplant varieties with a day count, 82.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 15.52 t/ha trails the average of its group, 20.34. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit eggplant fields most often: [eggplant fruit and shoot borer](/pests/eggplant-fruit-and-shoot-borer), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
It is dark purple to blackish and broad to oval.
Where and when to plant UPL Eg II eggplant

Buyers in each market want their own talong: long and slim and dark purple in most of Luzon, rounder or striped in some towns. Pick a variety with bacterial wilt resistance, and plan for the fruit and shoot borer whatever you plant, because no variety on the market resists it. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 79 to 86 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 15.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of UPL Eg II?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
